summary: ARES-7 (Redline Outpost) is an interactive, web-based 3D resource-management simulation that challenges young learners ages 7–12 to keep a Martian outpost and its crew safe across seven sols. Built for the Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge, the game turns static space-science concepts into hands-on systems thinking. Using real NASA space-weather and Mars mission data, players balance limited solar power across Life Support, Radiation Shielding, and a Bio-Dome while experiencing how every survival decision creates trade-offs.
details:
What It Does & Why It Matters Static science lessons explain space hazards in isolation, making it hard for young learners to see how subsystems on a Martian habitat depend on one another. ARES-7 places students in the role of a mission operator at Jezero Crater over seven sols, showing how protecting one subsystem—such as boosting radiation shielding during a solar flare—puts immediate pressure on power, food, oxygen, and water reserves.

How It Works (4-Step Learning Loop)

1. Plan: Allocate limited solar energy (in 5 kW steps) across three core stations: Shield/Comms, Bio-Dome, and Habitat Life Support. 2. Execute: Run the sol and experience dynamic resource consumption, crop growth thresholds, and real solar flare radiation hazards. 3. Learn: Inspect crew health, supply levels, and an interactive "Why-Chain" that explains the exact cause-and-effect behind every outcome. 4. Improve: Use Coach Hints or two built-in replays to test a better survival strategy.

Creativity, Accessibility & Dual-Audience Design ARES-7 is built for two distinct audiences: Cadet Mode provides friendly language and hints for ages 7–12, while Judge Mode reveals underlying formulas, data badges, and model limits so reviewers can distinguish measured NASA data from gameplay scaling. It also includes a 60-sec Judge demo mode, a Teacher & NGSS Guide, printable mission reports, and Simple View (an accessible non-3D mode supporting touch, mouse, and keyboard controls).

Tools, Languages & Architecture Built with TypeScript, Vite, and Three.js (hosted on Vercel), backed by Supabase (PostgreSQL, Authentication, and Row-Level Security) to store player progress, sol-by-sol mission histories, and NASA DONKI space-weather events with a reliable offline fallback catalog.
